validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification/duplicate/ownership — see separate spec and attribution concerns below.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of the sheet's own wiki citations. Kazinform (inform.kz, 2022) reports a scheduled Aug 1-25 2022 shutdown of the 'Kartaly-Rudny main gas pipeline' for corrosion repairs, calling it 'one of the first gas pipelines put into operation in Kazakhstan' and stating it has run continuously since 1965. Naша Газета/ng.kz (26 Jul 2024, quoting QazaqGaz deputy chairman Akbar Tulegenov at the Kostanay INVEST-2024 forum) states the pipeline 'Kartaly-Rudny' currently delivers the LARGEST share of gas reaching Kostanai region, is 1960s-built, single-line, and runs almost continuously -- and is the explicit reason QazaqGaz is building a $1B+ replacement line (CS-14 Bukhara-Ural, Aktobe -> Kostanai city, 630 km, 4.1 bcm/y, Qatari JV with Power International Holding/UCC Holding, 2023-2026) for energy-security diversification. A Kazakhstan government ecology public-hearing filing (hearings.ndbecology.gov.kz, doc 214986 -- a 2019-era reconstruction project for the pipeline's underwater crossing of the Karatomar reservoir at km 154-155) independently documents the same asset: 'Введен в эксплуатацию в 1965 г.' (commissioned 1965), serviced by Kostanai LPU, near the village Naberezhny, with cathodic-protection stations at km 151 and km 156. Intergas Central Asia's own 2015 KASE-filed annual report (kase.kz/files/emitters/INCA/incap_2015_rus.pdf) lists 'Карталы - Рудный' among UMG Kostanai's assets and, separately, 'Карталы-Рудный-Кустанай' in its system-inventory table at 1965/1,6 bcm-y design/0,461 bcm actual (28.8% utilization). This is a real, actively-monitored, currently-operating trunk line -- no existence concern. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk line (all sources call it 'магистральный газопровод'/main gas pipeline), not a gathering/feeder line -- confirmed. DUPLICATE: checked against the 39-pipeline Kazakhstan-gas roster; no other row shares this route or these endpoints (Kartaly/Chelyabinsk Oblast Russia -> Rudny -> Kostanai) -- unique, not a double-count. OWNERSHIP CHAIN: Intergas Central Asia's 2015 annual report traces its own share history (Intergas International B.V. -> KazTransGaz 2010 -> ultimately KazMunayGas/Samruk-Kazyna); intergas.kz's current 'About the company' page states in English: 'The Company is a subsidiary of the National Company QazaqGaz, JSC' -- confirms GEM's Owner1=QazaqGaz 100% is the CURRENT correct entity (QazaqGaz being the post-2021 successor once the gas transmission arm was carved out of KazMunayGas/KazTransGaz per this project's own country notes), and confirms Operator='AO Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya' is correct. Both intergas.kz pages I cite are the same origin as the operator's own self-report (medium tier alone), but the fact of Intergas as operator/QazaqGaz as parent is also implicit in ng.kz's independent framing of 'QazaqGaz' as the national operator responsible for this exact pipeline's replacement -- so tier medium-high overall on ownership.

validity.recommendation: Verify Capacity — Intergas's own audited 2015 annual report states a design capacity of only 1.6 bcm/y for this exact pipeline (with 0.461 bcm actual 2015 throughput, 28.8% utilization), not 5.36 bcm/y. No source was found supporting 5.36. Route to Update for correction or a second corroborating source before treating 5.36 as safe.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM: Capacity=5.36 bcm/y. Intergas Central Asia's own 2015 KASE-filed annual report (kase.kz/files/emitters/INCA/incap_2015_rus.pdf, system-inventory table) gives, for '«Карталы-Рудный-Кустанай», 1965': design capacity 1,6 млрд. м3 в год (1.6 bcm/y), actual 2015 throughput 0,461 млрд. м3 (0.461 bcm), utilization 28.8%. This is the SAME operator, SAME pipeline (identical 1965 start year, adjacent region text names it interchangeably 'Карталы - Рудный' at 155.8 km), and its own audited figure is under a third of GEM's 5.36. I could not find any independent source stating 5.36 bcm/y for this line. Regional context from ng.kz (2024): total Kostanai region gas consumption is ~1 bcm/y today, and this old pipeline supplies the largest share of it -- a design capacity in the 1.6-2 bcm/y range is more consistent with that consumption picture than 5.36 (which would imply the region uses only ~19% of available capacity, an unusually low utilization even by this line's own historical 28.8% baseline). Flagging as a material spec conflict per standing rule 4/5 rather than silently accepting the sheet value; not proposing a corrected number since I only have ONE primary source for 1.6 and it disagrees with the sheet — needs Update-workflow adjudication, ideally with a second source (e.g. a post-2019 reconstruction capacity upgrade record) before changing the cell.

validity.recommendation: Verify Length. GEM's own row name is 'Kartaly-Rudny-KOSTANAI' but its LengthKnown (155.8 km) matches Intergas's OWN internal figure for the shorter name 'Kartaly-Rudny' (no Kostanai) used elsewhere in the SAME 2015 annual report; that report's own summary table gives 227 km for '«Карталы-Рудный-Кустанай»' -- the full-name match. Compounding this, this session's route-integrity QC already flagged the drawn route geometry at ~600 km (ratio 3.85 vs the 155.8 km sheet value, RouteAccuracy currently 'high') -- so neither 155.8 nor 227 matches the drawn route either. Recommend Update resolve length AND route together, not length alone.
validity.researcher_notes: Intergas Central Asia's 2015 annual report (kase.kz/files/emitters/INCA/incap_2015_rus.pdf) is internally inconsistent on this exact asset within the SAME document: (1) in prose describing UMG Kostanai's assets, it names 'МГ «Бухара - Урал» в 3х ниточном исполнении (128,7 км), «Карталы - Рудный» (155,8 км), общая протяженность которых составляет – 284,5 км' -- i.e. 'Kartaly-Rudny' (no 'Kostanai' in the name) = 155.8 km, matching GEM's current value exactly; (2) in its system-inventory table it separately lists '«Карталы-Рудный-Кустанай», 1965, 227 км, 1,6 млрд. м3 в год' -- i.e. 'Kartaly-Rudny-Kostanai' (matching GEM's full row NAME) = 227 km, a 71.2 km/1.46x difference from 155.8. Both entries share the identical 1965 start year, so they are almost certainly the same physical asset described at two different route extents (the table's longer name/length may include the final leg into Kostanai city that the shorter prose figure excludes). This project's own QC pass (batches/kazakhstan-gas/staging/qc/route_integrity.json, check=length_ratio) already independently flagged that GEM's drawn route for P3955 measures a geodesic ~600 km against the sheet's 155.8 km (ratio 3.85, outside the 0.75-1.33 tolerance), noting 'wrong route, wrong length value, or a partial segment drawn' -- and 600 km doesn't match either 155.8 or 227 either, so the route geometry itself likely needs separate correction regardless of which length figure is adopted. Recommending a combined length+route review rather than a one-line length fix.

validity.recommendation: Correct FuelSource. 'Karachaganak Oil and Gas Field, Ural' is almost certainly a copy-paste artifact from the roster's OTHER Kazakhstan pipeline sourced from Karachaganak (P3947 Karachaganak-Uralsk Gas Pipeline: Karachaganak -> West Kazakhstan). P3955's actual gas source, per an independent news source, is imported Russian gas, tapped off the Bukhara-Ural trunk system at the Kartaly compressor station -- not the Karachaganak field, which is ~1,000+ km away in West Kazakhstan and cannot plausibly feed a pipeline whose start point is in Chelyabinsk Oblast, Russia.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM FuelSource='Karachaganak Oil and Gas Field, Ural'. This is geographically implausible: P3955's own StartLocation/StartState-Province/StartCountryOrArea fields (Kartaly, Kartalinsky District, Chelyabinsk region, RUSSIA) place its source point in Russia, ~1,000+ km from the Karachaganak field in West Kazakhstan (which feeds the roster's SEPARATE P3947 Karachaganak-Uralsk Gas Pipeline, Karachaganak -> West Kazakhstan, cap 0.5 bcm/y) -- gas cannot flow from Karachaganak to Kartaly against/across the existing pipeline grid without an unrecorded, implausible detour. Independent confirmation of the true source: ng.kz (26 Jul 2024, on-record quote from QazaqGaz deputy chairman) states plainly of this exact pipeline, 'газ поступает российский' (the gas is Russian), citing this as the specific energy-security vulnerability motivating the new replacement pipeline. A separate open-web search independently corroborates the mechanism: 'КС Карталы' (Kartaly compressor station) is a linear station ON the Bukhara-Ural (Бухара-Урал) trunk pipeline, which transits Central Asian (Uzbek/Turkmen-origin) gas through Kazakhstan into Russia -- meaning Kartaly is the point where gas is tapped back OFF the Bukhara-Ural/Russian transit system into Kazakhstan via this branch line, consistent with 'Russian gas' framing even though its ultimate origin traces further back to Central Asia. Either way, 'Karachaganak Oil and Gas Field' is not a plausible fuel source for this line. I did not find a primary source naming the exact originating Russian field/system precisely enough to propose a specific replacement value (no fabrication per standing rule 2) -- recommending the cell be corrected to something in the family of 'Imported (Russian gas grid, via Bukhara-Ural system tapped at Kartaly)' pending a source that names it more precisely.

validity.recommendation: No change recommended, but note the nominal-vs-outer-diameter ambiguity for future reference.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM Diameter='700, 820' mm. A Kazakhstan government ecology public-hearing filing (hearings.ndbecology.gov.kz, doc 214986, a real 2019-era reconstruction project for this exact pipeline's Karatomar reservoir crossing at km 154-155) documents this exact line's mainline pipe as 'Д720 мм' (720mm, standard Soviet/Russian large-diameter trunk-pipe OD) with a 'Ду 700' (DN700 nominal-bore) valve installed on it -- both numbers describing the SAME physical pipe from different diameter conventions (720mm outer vs. ~700mm nominal/inner bore after wall thickness). GEM's other Kazakhstan-gas rows consistently record actual OUTER diameter (508, 530, 813, 1020, 1220mm are literal Soviet-standard OD sizes), so P3955's '700' may be a transcription of the nominal/valve-bore figure rather than the pipe's true 720mm OD -- a minor precision note, not a material error, since both 700 and 720 are real, independently documented technical facts about this exact line. '820' (also a standard Soviet OD size) is plausible for a different, later-built segment but I found no independent source specifically confirming it. NOTE: url_verifier.py returned a content-check FAIL (200, 'missing expected') on this hearing PDF -- confirmed by direct download this is a false negative of the documented large/non-standard-font-PDF class (script docstring): `pdftotext -layout` on the downloaded file finds 'Карталы-Рудный' dozens of times in clean, readable Cyrillic text, including the exact passages quoted here. Citing per the same standing precedent already used elsewhere in this project (large-PDF content-check false negatives, e.g. OPEC ASB).

fills.researcher_notes: Kazinform (2022, independent news agency): pipeline operating continuously since 1965 (article frames the 2022 shutdown as the first major interruption in '57 years'). Intergas's own 2015 annual report system-inventory table independently lists '«Карталы-Рудный-Кустанай», 1965'. Two independent origins agreeing on the exact same year -> high tier.

Status inferred from context, not a literal 'operating' string match (per confidence_tiers guidance). ng.kz (Jul 2024) describes the pipeline as CURRENTLY delivering the largest share of Kostanai region's gas ('Сегодня наибольший объем газа поступает... по... «Карталы-Рудный»'). inform.kz (2022) frames a scheduled repair shutdown against a backdrop of otherwise near-continuous operation ('эксплуатируется практически беспрерывно' echoed again in the 2024 piece). Both confirm active operating status as of their publication dates.
Explicitly and repeatedly called a 'магистральный газопровод' (main GAS pipeline) in both sources.
'Магистральный' = trunk/transmission (as opposed to a gathering/distribution line); confirmed correctly classified, not a gathering or feeder line.

Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than sourcing the sheet's 5.36 -- the only primary figure I found (Intergas's own 2015 annual report design capacity, 1.6 bcm/y) CONTRADICTS the sheet value rather than supporting it. See validity concern (spec/capacity) above.

155.8 km DOES appear verbatim in the operator's own 2015 report -- but attached there to the shorter name 'Kartaly-Rudny' (no Kostanai), while the SAME report's summary table gives 227 km for the full-name 'Kartaly-Rudny-Kostanai' match, and this session's own route-integrity QC flags the drawn route at ~600 km. Marking UNRESOLVED rather than REFS_ADDED because the value is real but its scope/match to this row's full name is ambiguous -- see validity concern (spec/length) above.

Government ecology hearing filing for this exact pipeline's river-crossing reconstruction confirms Д720мм mainline pipe with Ду700 valving on this line (the 700/720 nominal-vs-outer nuance is flagged separately as a caveat, not a correction). 820mm segment not independently confirmed -- partial support only, single source, tier medium not high. url_verifier's automated content-check FAILed on this PDF (large/non-standard-font extraction false negative, documented in url_verifier.py's own docstring for this PDF class); verified genuine and on-topic via manual pdftotext -layout extraction, which surfaces the exact passages quoted.

summary: P3955 is a real, actively-operating trunk line (Kartaly, Chelyabinsk Oblast Russia -> Rudny -> Kostanai, since 1965) with correct classification/ownership and no duplicate, BUT: Capacity (5.36 bcm/y) conflicts with the operator's own 2015 annual report (1.6 bcm/y design, 0.461 bcm actual) -- concern/spec, UNRESOLVED; Length (155.8 km) matches only the shorter 'Kartaly-Rudny' name in that same report while the full-name match gives 227 km, and the drawn route measures ~600 km per this session's own QC flag -- concern/spec, UNRESOLVED; FuelSource ('Karachaganak Oil and Gas Field, Ural') is a likely copy-paste error from P3947 -- independent reporting confirms this line's gas is Russian-sourced via the Bukhara-Ural system at Kartaly, not Karachaganak -- concern/attribution. Start/Status/Fuel/PipelineType filled with high-tier independent refs; Diameter partially corroborated (medium).
